pairs.title: Raw / escaped output
pairs.interpretation: Per-file ICFG is not a taint graph; htmlspecialchars remains visible but sanitisation is not proved.

pairs.title: Direct / dynamic call
pairs.interpretation: The concatenated function-name assignment remains, but no constant propagation resolves the dynamic call target.

pairs.title: Direct / callback
pairs.interpretation: call_user_func receives risk 1 even with a fixed harmless callback.

pairs.title: Plain / namespaced function
pairs.interpretation: Flattening restores statements but discards namespace context.

pairs.title: Try-catch / linear
pairs.interpretation: Flattening serialises alternative exception paths; an ICFG equality is not semantic equivalence.

pairs.title: Local variable rename
pairs.interpretation: Normalisation removes local identifier differences; this does not establish preservation of data dependence.

pairs.title: Whitespace inside string
pairs.interpretation: Deleting all whitespace in raw bytes can collapse semantically distinct string literals.

pairs.title: Closure / arrow function
pairs.interpretation: Closures are hoisted; arrow functions are not independently lowered by this extractor.

pairs.title: Fixed / escaped argument
pairs.interpretation: Both legitimate fixed-command examples receive critical risk; risk does not encode authorisation or argument safety.

pairs.title: Plain / encoded constant
pairs.interpretation: Encoding alone does not receive obfuscated risk; the extractor never decodes strings into code.

pairs.title: Different input dependencies
pairs.interpretation: Pruning the constant assignment and mapping distinct local variables to one name makes two different input dependencies share a normalised graph.
